standard_prerequisites.use: After the reduction to an affine base it is exactly the asserted equality $\mathcal{I}f_*\mathcal{F} = f_*(f^{-1}\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F})$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of the inverse image functor, which makes the inverse image of an ideal a sheaf of ideals
standard_prerequisites.use: It shows that $f^{-1}\mathcal{I}$ is a sheaf of ideals of $f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_X$, acting on $\mathcal{F}$ through $f^\sharp$, so that $f^{-1}\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F}$ makes sense.

core_obligations: Spell out the notation: $f^{-1}\mathcal{I}$ is a sheaf of ideals of $f^{-1}\mathcal{O}_X$ acting on $\mathcal{F}$ via $f^\sharp$, and $f^{-1}\mathcal{I}\mathcal{F}$ is the subsheaf generated by local sections of the form $as$ (proof lines 3396-3402).
Note that this subsheaf is quasi-coherent as the image of the natural map $f^*\mathcal{I} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y} \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}$ (proof lines 3402-3404).
Reduce the claim to the case where $X$ is an affine scheme, the question being etale local on $X$, and apply the corresponding statement for schemes (proof lines 3406-3409).
proof_roadmap: The notation and quasi-coherence of the subsheaf (proof lines 3396-3404).
Reduction to an affine base (proof lines 3406-3408).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the ideal multiple of a pushforward along an affine morphism with the pushforward of the submodule generated by the inverse image ideal, with the notation carefully explained (statement lines 3385-3393). The proof spells out the action of the inverse image ideal, observes that the generated submodule is quasi-coherent as the image of a natural map, and reduces etale locally on the target to the scheme case. The notation and the locality reduction are the substance, so the claim is H2.
